content: Granules used for mosquito larval control can be applied from aircraft or with motorized knapsack sprayers that are adapted for granular application. However, manually carried granular applicators specifically designed for mosquito control are not commonly available. Various designs of manually carried granular applicators, originally intended for agricultural use, can be repurposed for mosquito larval control. Insecticides formulated as granules for this purpose differ in size, composition, and recommended application rates, necessitating calibration of each type of equipment with the specific insecticide product prior to field use. General Requirements for Granular Applicators: 1. Materials: All materials used in the construction of granular applicators must resist corrosion and chemical degradation, ensuring durability and proper functioning during normal use. 2. Design: The applicator must be designed to prevent granules from being trapped or retained on its outer surfaces. All fittings should be free of sharp edges or projections to avoid injury to operators. 3. Weight: The maximum weight of the applicator, when filled to its recommended capacity, must comply with national health and safety regulations. In the absence of such regulations, the weight should not exceed 25 kg for knapsack models or 20 kg for hand-carried models. 4. Hopper: The hopper must have a tight lid to prevent spillage and dust escape. It should not be mounted in front of the operator and must allow complete emptying. For small equipment with hopper openings less than 90 mm wide, a funnel or closed transfer system should be used for filling. 5. Flow Control: A device must regulate the quantity of granules released, either as a single dose or for broader area distribution. 6. Straps: Straps on manually carried equipment must be wide enough (50 mm ± 5 mm) to avoid discomfort, adjustable in length, and durable enough to pass drop tests. 7. Markings: Equipment must clearly display the manufacturer’s name, contact details, machine type, date of manufacture, serial number, and key operational components. The type of granules suitable for use must also be indicated. Markings must remain legible despite exposure to pesticides. 8. User Manual: A clear, illustrated manual must accompany the equipment, detailing operation, calibration, safety precautions, maintenance, and spare parts. It should also specify granule sizes, dosage ranges, and application methods (area or spot application). Specific Types of Granular Applicators: 1. Manually Carried (Shoulder-Mounted) Applicators: These consist of a shoulder-slung bag made of rubberized or neoprene-treated material with a delivery tube. The bag must have a zippered opening for easy filling and a tapered metal discharge tube at its lowest point. A flow adjustment device must be included within the tube. The fully loaded unit must not exceed 12 kg. Granules are applied by swinging the discharge tube side-to-side in a pattern to evenly distribute granules over a 7-meter swath. 2. Hand-Carried Applicators: These consist of a tube containing granules that fall by gravity to an outlet. A hand-operated mechanism allows a fixed quantity of granules to be released. The granule-holding section must have a wider opening than the delivery tube for easy filling and be fitted with a lid to prevent spillage. The tube diameter must be at least 70 mm, and the fully loaded unit must not exceed 5 kg. The unit is designed for precise application to discrete breeding sites. 3. Knapsack Granular Applicators: These consist of a container allowing granules to fall by gravity to a delivery tube held in front of the user. The container must have a large opening (minimum 12 cm diameter) for quick filling and an inset filter to prevent debris entry. A tight lid must prevent dust escape, and the container should be mounted on a frame with comfortable straps for the operator’s back. The delivery tube must include a dose regulator and an on/off valve, with optional devices for granule spreading. 4. Motorized Knapsack Mist Blowers Adapted for Granule Distribution: These units include a container above an engine-driven fan that produces a high-velocity airstream to project granules over a swath of at least 5 meters. The engine must have an easy-start mechanism, a fuel tank below it, and guards for moving parts and exhaust to prevent operator injury. Engine controls, including a stop switch and speed control, must be visible to the operator. A padded backrest and vibration-dampening engine mounting are required for operator comfort. The granule container must have a wide inlet (minimum 120 mm) with a mesh filter and a tight lid. Additional Requirements: Durability: Applicators must withstand at least 50 hours of operation over 10 days, including one 8-hour session, without significant stoppages or failures. Noise Level: Equipment producing noise levels exceeding 85 decibels must be labeled to indicate the need for ear protection. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): Operators and maintenance personnel must use appropriate PPE, such as coveralls, gloves, face masks, and footwear, to minimize pesticide exposure. International standards for protective clothing and equipment must be adhered to. Testing and Standards: Applicators must undergo corrosion and chemical resistance tests to ensure material durability. Tanks must pass fatigue tests to withstand repeated pressurizations without leakage or failure. Equipment must comply with ISO standards for crop protection and pesticide application equipment. This detailed guidance ensures the safe, effective, and environmentally responsible use of granular applicators in vector control programs.
